correctness.rationale: The intrinsic taxicab quotient ball is the projection of all translates of the covering-space diamond. The map (x,y)↦(x+y,x−y) takes that diamond to a side-2r square and the integer periods to the same-parity lattice in the two new coordinates. The vertical coordinate modulo 1 has circle fibers with raw horizontal period 2. For 0<2r<1 each square has one vertical lift over an active fiber and no lift otherwise, so it contributes an interval of coordinate length 2r; its active set has measure 2r on the base circle. Covering a fiber of length 2 forces at least ceil(1/r) active centers, and integrating gives 2rN≥ceil(1/r), with the stated final ceiling. The bound implies N≥4 for r<1/2; it strictly beats the integer area bound, for example throughout [1/√6,1/2). For r=1/(2n), in the transformed plane the claimed center lattice is the side-2r square grid containing the period lattice; its index in the quotient is 2n² since the areas are 2 and (2r)². This tiles and also attains the projected-area lower bound. The construction at n=1 works without the strict slice hypothesis. Diameter 1 rules out one center below 1, and two centers cover at and above 1/2. Thus the two and three center optima are 1/2, even though N is never 3. The supplied exact rational script was read, not executed; its grid checks do not prove a continuum cover.
residual_risks: This proof concerns closed balls in the intrinsic sum metric, with unrestricted centers. It does not compute the whole sub-half covering function or apply to Euclidean circles or general torus lattices.

value.rationale: An exact missing cardinality for the smallest nontrivial sum-metric circle product is a motivated sharp threshold, not a sample or direct area estimate. Slice integrality excludes three even where area allows it, and the infinite family shows saturation. The obstruction is already useful as a baseline for separating subsequent small-center phases. The scientific gain is the integer obstruction and its sharp consequences, not the use of an ordinary parallelogram tiling by itself.
residual_risks: No completeness, optimizer classification, or general product-covering conjecture is claimed.
